meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa (International Company regime under the International Companies Act 1987)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English common law heritage, with customary law elements recognized by the Constitution of Samoa 1962)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: China–Samoa Bilateral Investment Treaty — Agreement on the Promotion and Protection of Investments (in force)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER Plus) — regional FTA (in force)
Samoa–EU interim Economic Partnership Agreement (iEPA) — trade/development agreement
Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) with Australia, New Zealand, Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland and Iceland (not full DTAAs)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended (incl. International Companies (Amendment) Act 2011 and subsequent amendments), ss. 7, 60, 122-124A (registered office, registered agent, registers and beneficial-ownership due diligence); Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (Samoa), as amended by the Money Laundering Prevention (Amendment) Act 2017; Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) of Samoa AML/CFT directives; FATF Recommendation 24 implementing obligations for licensed registered agents.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport / national ID of each shareholder, director, secretary and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence; foreign documents authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (English original; Chinese version for PRC shareholders)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporation service provider / Samoan licensed registered agent; document must be lodged with the Registrar of International Companies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and professional introduction (client due diligence reference)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or regulated professional firm (lawyer/accountant)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney in favor of the Samoan licensed registered agent / incorporation service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in country of signing; endorsed by the Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or corporate extract (for corporate shareholders/UBOs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies of the corporate shareholder's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration / source of wealth and source of funds statement (AML/CFT form)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Samoan registered agent, with notarized signature of the UBO

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based KYC/EDD screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, settlors, beneficiaries and UBOs against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT sanctions list, and Samoa FIU advisories; mandatory PEP identification based on nationality, residence, and political/business exposure, including family members and close associates; enhanced due diligence and source-of-funds verification required for any PEP or sanctions flag under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and FIU Samoa guidance; negative news and adverse-media screening required prior to incorporation and on an ongoing basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies and International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) — Apia; online name-availability check via https://www.mcil.gov.ws and filings submitted exclusively through a licensed Samoan registered agent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under s. 7 of the International Companies Act 1987, the name of an International Company may be in Latin letters or Chinese characters (or a combined Latin/Chinese form) and must end with 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated' or an approved abbreviation ('Ltd', 'Corp', 'Inc'); where a Chinese-character name is used, the Registrar requires a Pinyin transliteration or English translation for name-conflict and public-record purposes; the Latin-script name shall be the primary official name; names must not be misleading, identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The registered agent files a name-availability search and reservation request with the Registrar of International Companies. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may, within 14 days of the rejection notice, file a written administrative objection with the Registrar through the registered agent. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may petition the Chief Executive Officer of the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour for ministerial review and, thereafter, apply to the Supreme Court of Samoa for judicial review. A fresh name reservation (new 30-day window) is required for any alternative name submitted after rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this non-licensed, cloud-software International Company (ISIC 6201 fintech app): the statutory registered office must be the physical Apia office of the licensed Samoan registered agent, and the company may maintain no physical business premises in Samoa; all operations, data hosting and client management may be conducted remotely. A virtual office cannot replace the statutory registered office, which must accept service of process during normal business hours.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — quantified at approximately 5–10% annual probability for a remotely operated, non-licensed IC with no Samoan business assets; Registrar/FIU inspection powers under the International Companies Act 1987 and MLP Act 2007 are primarily exercised against licensed registered agents and their records rather than the IC's overseas business site.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended; ss. 5–9 (incorporation application), s. 10 (certificate of incorporation), s. 11 (registered office and agent), ss. 54–60 (directors and first board powers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Companies & Trusts Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 – Application for Incorporation of an International Company, together with executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement; no escrow or capital deposit rule. The company may allot one or more shares with a nominal par value fixed by the Memorandum; no paid-in capital verification is required by the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED that the incorporation of this International Company under the International Companies Act 1987 be and is hereby ratified in all respects; that one hundred (100) ordinary shares of US$1.00 each are allotted to the founding subscriber, fully paid by book entry in the Company's share capital ledger. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office established in Apia, Samoa, together with the duly licensed registered agent, be adopted as the Company's statutory seat and agent of record. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Director] be and is hereby appointed Sole Director and [Secretary] is appointed Company Secretary, each authorized severally to open bank accounts, execute commercial agreements, procure the corporate seal, and submit obligatory returns to the Registrar for the conduct of the Company's software and financial portfolio tracking business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Registered Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies & Trusts Registry, MCIL (online filing window and registry counter, Apia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name availability search through a licensed Samoa registered agent; reserve the proposed company name and concurrently execute the Registered Agent Engagement Letter undertaking to maintain the registered office and statutory registers in Apia.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and suffix (IC or Limited)
Registered agent engagement letter executed by the agent
Identification copy of the incorporator or authorized filer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as undesirable or confusingly similar, submit a revised name or appeal in writing to the Registrar for administrative review within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application with Memorandum and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies & Trusts Registry, MCIL
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute and lodge Form 1 together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association, subscriber statements, and director consents. The registered agent countersigns to confirm compliance with the International Companies Act 1987; the Registry assesses and issues an acknowledgment.
required_dossiers: Form 1 – Application for Incorporation
Memorandum and Articles of Association (executed and notarized if required by the agent)
Consent of the proposed director(s) and registered agent
Passport copy and proof of residential address of each subscriber
Name reservation confirmation letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Registry issues a query notice listing deficiencies; the filer corrects and resubmits within 14 days. If the application is rejected, a fresh application with revised constitutional documents may be lodged, preserving the reserved name for 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Government Fees and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Treasury Division, Ministry of Finance, and Samoa International Companies & Trusts Registry, MCIL
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon assessment, pay the prescribed filing fee by bank transfer to the Registry's trust account; present the payment receipt to the Registry counter, which then issues the Certificate of Incorporation, corporate seal, and tax-exemption certificate (if applicable).
required_dossiers: Registry fee assessment notice
Bank payment confirmation / receipt
Acknowledgment of incorporation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is misapplied or the certificate is withheld, provide the certified bank credit advice to the Registry's inspection unit and escalate to the Assistant Registrar for expedited release.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Share Allotment, and Officer Appointment Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors in conjunction with the registered agent; subsequent filing with Samoa International Companies & Trusts Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting by unanimous written resolution; allot shares to the founding subscriber; appoint the sole director and company secretary; adopt the registered office; and cause the registered agent to file the Notice of Director and Registered Office particulars with the Registry.
required_dossiers: Signed first board resolution (as set out in the legal framework)
Share transfer / allotment ledger entry
Register of members and register of directors
Notice of director, secretary, and registered office (Form 2 equivalent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries officer details, re-execute the resolution and file an amended notice with corrected particulars; late or defective filings may be cured upon payment of the nominal reinstatement fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Local Business Licence, Fire Safety Certification, and Premises Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour – Licensing and Commerce Division; Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA); Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Commercial Business Licence for software and cloud analytics services because the company maintains a physical office in Samoa; arrange fire safety inspection of the registered premises; and obtain an occupancy/structural clearance from the building authority for the leased office floor.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Commercial lease agreement for the registered premises
Completed business licence application form
Fire safety and evacuation compliance statement
Building occupancy / structural safety certificate from MWTI
Director and staff identification for occupational registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the business licence is refused, correct the premises compliance deficiencies, submit remedial evidence, and request re-inspection within 10 working days; a further administrative appeal lies to the Registrar of Companies and the Ministry of Commerce.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Licensing and Commerce Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Samoa Commercial Business Licence (General Software and Cloud Analytics Services)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Division of Environment and Conservation, Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Tier 3 Registration Only. Non-industrial office use with no Schedule A activity under the Environment Act 2003; the company must file an environmental registration statement with the Division, but no full EIA Report or Environmental Permit is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial process effluent; office sanitary wastewater discharges only to the municipal sewer system in Apia with pH 6.0–9.0 and TSS below 250 mg/L per Samoa wastewater regulations; no VOC or chemical emissions from operations; electronic and inert office waste segregated and handed to a licensed waste hauler in compliance with the Waste Management (Samoa) Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety and emergency evacuation certificate issued by the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA); structural load and occupancy clearance for the leased office floor issued by the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI); workplace electrical installation safety inspection; and occupational health registration of all employees under the Samoa Occupational Safety and Health Act 1983 (as amended).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue, Independent State of Samoa (Samoa Revenue Department), Apia; official administration portal: www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign investors incorporating a Samoa International Company obtain a Certificate of Incorporation from the Samoa International Companies and Foreign Companies Registry (SICR). For administrative identification, the Ministry for Revenue automatically assigns a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) upon registration of the company with the SICR. A separate VAGST identification number is required only where the International Company makes taxable supplies in Samoa and exceeds the WST 100,000 annual turnover threshold, in which case the foreign entity must apply for VAGST registration with the Ministry for Revenue, submitting the certificate of incorporation, statutory forms, and certified copies of identification of directors and shareholders. Where the International Company conducts wholly offshore activities, it generally receives a Certificate of Tax Exempt Status and is not required to file Samoan income tax returns, though it must maintain records of its offshore nature.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa International Companies are automatically classified as tax-exempt offshore entities and are excluded from Samoan income tax, stamp duty, exchange control, and VAGST on offshore transactions. There is no check-the-box election comparable to US tax classification. An International Company may elect under the International Companies Act 1987 to cancel its international status and re-domicile as a domestic company, thereby becoming subject to ordinary Samoan corporate taxation. Samoa has not enacted hybrid mismatch or transparent entity election rules; no similar statutory election mechanism exists for International Companies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period; voluntary registration permitted for WST 60,000 or more
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time electronic fiscal clearance, API reporting, or digital stamping mandate exists under Samoan law. Registered suppliers must issue a valid VAGST tax invoice containing statutory particulars (supplier name, VAGST registration number, date of supply, description, tax-exclusive value, and VAGST charged). E-invoicing is permissible in PDF or XML format but does not require pre-clearance by the Ministry for Revenue.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Samoa are zero-rated where the exporter retains evidence of export within the statutory time limit, ordinarily 28 days from the date of supply, and the goods leave Samoa to a destination outside Samoa. Services are zero-rated where the recipient is a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time the services are performed and the benefit of the services is wholly outside Samoa. International Companies engaged exclusively in offshore financial portfolio tracking and similar fintech services are not within the Samoan VAGST net; consequently they are not required to charge output VAT and no formal zero-rating claim is necessary.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Samoan Customs Service CUSEX Form)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill issued to the overseas buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer evidence in foreign currency
Commercial invoice and packing list evidencing Samoa origin
Certificate of Origin where preferential tariff treatment is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry for Revenue may audit zero-rated export claims retrospectively for up to 10 years where there is fraud or willful evasion, and 5 years in other cases. Where documentary substantiation is inadequate, the entire zero-rated output tax is clawed back as VAGST due, together with a late-payment penalty of 2% per month and an automatic penalty of 100% of the tax avoided for fraudulent misdeclaration. Directors and persons involved in facilitating a false zero-rating claim may be personally liable and subject to criminal prosecution under the VAGST Act 2008 and the Samoa Crimes Act 2013, resulting in fines up to WST 100,000 and imprisonment up to seven years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), Exchange Control and AML/CFT Supervision Division, with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) acting as the statutory registry and licensing authority for International Companies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is not a freely convertible offshore currency; current-account payments for services, software subscriptions, and trade are processed by licensed authorised dealers on presentation of underlying contracts and invoices. Capital-account transactions, including non-resident equity injections and shareholder loan repayments, require Central Bank of Samoa approval if settled in WST. An International Company operating under the Tax-Exempt Zone may lawfully hold and transact foreign-currency accounts in USD, EUR, AUD, and NZD through licensed commercial banks without conversion to WST, provided it conducts no domestic Samoan business. Profit remittance and dividend distribution to non-resident shareholders are permissible after submission of audited financial statements, a valid board dividend resolution, and comprehensive source-of-funds documentation; no withholding tax applies to offshore International Company dividends, but the paying bank will require enhanced beneficial-owner clearance for trust structures.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Samoa's Exchange Control Act and Central Bank directives, exporters of goods and services, including cross-border software and digital fintech services, must repatriate proceeds to Samoa within 30 days of receipt. The mandatory surrender ratio is 100% for proceeds intended to support domestic operating costs; however, authorised dealers may approve foreign-currency retention accounts in USD, EUR, AUD, or NZD allowing an exporter to retain up to 100% of export receipts for offshore treasury deployment and trade settlement, subject to monthly reconciliation with the Central Bank. For a non-resident International Company, the surrender obligation is administratively relaxed but not formally waived; all inward remittances must be tagged with the correct software/technology export purpose code and supported by service contracts and itemised invoices retained for CBS inspection.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and USD Operational Account
Operational Account with Foreign-Currency Retention Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for primary treasury reliance. Samoa does not issue standalone e-money institution licences without a commercial banking licence, and offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, Airwallex, or Mercury operate under foreign licences that are not reciprocally recognised by the Central Bank of Samoa. Such EMIs may be used as supplementary collection gateways for consumer payments, but the principal clearing account, regulatory nexus, and liquidity buffer must remain with a CBS-licensed commercial bank. Legal constraints prohibit routing Samoan-source WST conversions through unlicensed EMIs and require that all merchant settlement flows from Stripe and Apple IAP be consolidated into a licensed bank within the permitted end-of-day reconciliation window.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No blanket statutory requirement exists for directors to appear physically in Apia. ANZ and BSP generally permit remote account opening for International Companies using a live video interview with the compliance officer, certified passport copies, notarised corporate register, and SIFA certificate. At least one director or the ultimate beneficial owner must complete a live anti-money-laundering interview remotely; Samoa Commercial Bank may require physical attendance for higher-risk Chinese-family-office trust structures. The absence of a physical branch visit is acceptable if the bank can verify the registered office in Samoa, obtain a professional reference from a recognised overseas attorney or accountant, and conduct enhanced due diligence on all trust beneficiaries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex family-office trust structure with mainland-China, Hong Kong, or Singapore resident settlers and multiple layers of discretionary beneficiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the trust deed and trust registration certificate; certified passports of settlor, protector, trustees, and all named beneficiaries; 24-month source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; professional introduction letter from a licensed lawyer or accountant; notarised board resolutions appointing signatories; current SIFA certificate of good standing; completed bank KYC questionnaire; written explanations of any recent changes in beneficiaries or trust structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dependency on Stripe and Apple IAP as principal consumer payment rails, which may trigger e-money/payment-aggregator red flags or high-volume card-not-present risk classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed payment-provider merchant agreements; PCI DSS attestation of compliance for the cloud platform; standard terms of service and privacy policy; app store listing and product demonstration link; transaction-level monthly reconciliation exports; chargeback and refund analytics dashboard access; outside counsel opinion confirming the entity is a software-as-a-service provider and not a money-transmitter or unlicensed payment institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore tax-exempt International Company status combined with nominee officers indistinct from shell-company indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date shareholders ledger and directors register maintained at the Samoa registered office; declaration confirming no bearer shares are outstanding; written nominee agreements identifying every nominator and nominee; ultimate beneficial ownership chart with percentage ownership for every natural person; SIFA compliance confirmation letter; signed economic substance and compliance statement confirming the company will not trade domestically in Samoa; engagement letter from the Samoa licensed registered agent.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires a single SWIFT MT103 wire from the external shareholder's bank through a corresponding international bank to the beneficiary's foreign-currency account at ANZ or BSP in Samoa. The remittance must carry a transparent purpose code of 'Equity Injection', 'Direct Investment Capital Subscription', or the CBS-recognised capital transaction equivalent, with the beneficiary field showing the International Company legal name and account number. The supporting pack must include the board resolution approving the capital call, the shares subscription agreement, the certificate of incorporation, audited or management financials, and source-of-funds statement from the remitting shareholder. Funds should never be split into smaller transfers, routed through third-party wallets, or settled in cash; any deviation will trigger automatic AML suspicion and potential freezing by the correspondent bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 USD wire for non-documentary settlements such as software licensing fees, cloud infrastructure payments, legal retainers, and intercompany management fees. For physical goods or high-value trade arrangements, a commercial letter of credit issued by the Samoan authorised dealer bank is used, with documents including commercial invoice, bill of lading or air waybill, certificates of origin, and insurance certificate. Local Samoan Tala operating expenditures are cleared via the national RTGS and the bank's local transfer network. All outbound disbursements must be matched to supporting contracts and invoices, screened against UN, OFAC, EU, and Samoan sanctions lists at both the ordering and receiving banks, and recorded in the treasury ledger with the corresponding SWIFT reference.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts of up to 12 months against USD/WST, EUR/WST, AUD/WST, and NZD/WST with licensed Samoa authorised dealer banks, executed only to hedge receivables or payables arising from the software subscription business.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing WST, permitted only for hedging verifiable cross-border exposure and prohibited for speculative trading, with counterparty being a CBS-approved international bank and all profits or losses settled in convertible foreign currency.

Plain vanilla cross-currency swaps between USD, EUR, AUD, and NZD for treasury cash pooling and liquidity rebalancing, with a maturity not exceeding 5 years and with Central Bank notification required if any settlement leg involves the Samoan Tala.

Vanilla FX call and put options purchased from authorised dealer banks to protect highly probable forecasted foreign-currency inflows and outflows, where the notional amount is capped at 125% of the documented treasury exposure and no exotic or leveraged structures are permitted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of an International Company (Form A/R) including register continuation and no-local-business declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (via licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the appointed financial year-end; the default financial year-end is 31 December unless a different accounting reference date is filed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-filing monetary penalty accrues until lodged; continued arrears beyond 6 months expose the company to administrative strike-off, after which assets vest in the Registrar and restoration requires court approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Ultimate Beneficial Ownership and Registered Agent Certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit and Samoa International Companies Registry through licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the annual return; no separate extension beyond the annual return deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing constitutes a continuing AML/CFT regulatory breach, with fines imposed under the International Companies Act and AML/CFT Act scaled by corporate size; may suspend agent services and support involuntary strike-off action

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is not compulsory for a passive exempt International Company unless it has more than 10 members, holds client money or investment portfolios on a commercial basis, has issued securities to the public, or a shareholder holding at least 25% of voting rights validly requires an audit under the articles
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Samoa IFRS-equivalent accounting standards for any statutory or contractual financial statements; accounting records must correctly explain transactions and financial position at intervals not exceeding 6 months

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every transfer of shares is effective only on registration in the Register of Members; the registered agent must verify and record UBO changes at least annually at the filing date, updating percentage ownership of each individual holding 25% or more of shares or control

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for International Companies; ordinary Samoa resident companies are taxed at 27%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 100% statutory exemption from Samoa corporate income tax, capital gains tax, and stamp duty under the International Companies Act 1987; no tax on passive investment income or non-Samoan source income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No Samoa corporate income tax return is prescribed for International Companies. Annual compliance is satisfied by filing the International Company Annual Return with the Samoa International Companies Registry (SICR) through the Government of Samoa Companies Online Portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than the last day of the month following the anniversary of incorporation; annual registry fees are due on 31 March of each year for calendar-year registered companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name and International Company registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter exact name as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation; no Samoa tax reference number is required for tax-exempt ICs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address and licensed registered agent in Samoa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be a physical Samoa address maintained by a licensed international company service provider; non-resident directors cannot use a foreign address.
List all non-resident directors with passport numbers and country of residence; do not complete any Samoan tax residency declaration.
State number of issued shares and classes; nominee directorship or shareholdings may be declared to the registered agent for beneficial ownership registry purposes only.
The licensed agent must sign and attest that the IC is conducting a permitted offshore business and is not engaged in domestic Samoa trading.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return or late payment of the registry fee attracts a late surcharge of 10% per month or part-month, capped at 100% of the annual fee. Persistent default leads to automatic strike-off by the Registrar, restoration costs of approximately WST 1,000, and possible disqualification of the registered agent or director.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by an International Company to non-resident shareholders; the general Samoa non-resident dividend withholding tax rate is 15% under the Income Tax Act 2014 for ordinary resident companies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: International Companies are wholly exempt from Samoa withholding tax, so no DTA relief application or Samoan tax residence certificate (TRC) is required for outbound dividend distributions. If a general company were taxed and a treaty claim arose, the beneficial owner must submit a written DTA relief application and a valid Samoa TRC to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue before payment date to obtain the reduced treaty rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% under the International Company exemption; the statutory rate for ordinary Samoa companies is 15% for royalties and 15% for interest. Samoa double tax agreements generally provide for 0%-10% on interest and 0%-5% on royalties, subject to beneficial ownership and prior TRC clearance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable. Samoa International Companies are exempt from Samoa income tax and therefore outside the transfer pricing documentation regime. The Samoa Income Tax Act 2014 contains a general arm's length rule for connected-party cross-border transactions but prescribes no codified monetary threshold for IC compliance.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa does not apply Economic Substance Regulations. International Companies are not required to evidence substantial activity or local management in Samoa. The International Companies Act 1987 only requires a registered office and resident agent; passive financial portfolio holding and tracking activities are expressly permissible as offshore business.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Samoa International Company to conceal true beneficial ownership, suppress reportable income, or facilitate foreign tax evasion while the entity has no independent economic substance; filing false statements or declarations with the Samoa Registrar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies Act 1987 and the Income Tax Act 2014: fines up to WST 100,000 for false statements; assessed tax plus a penalty of up to 50% of the unpaid tax; strike-off and cancellation of the IC's registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are jointly and severally liable for fines, assessed taxes, and civil restitution. Culpable directors face imprisonment of up to 7 years, travel bans pending investigation, and disqualification from acting as directors of any Samoa-registered company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the entity as a bare nominee shell with no registered agent, no physical registered office, no accounting records, or falsely representing the IC as a domestic Samoa trading company to third parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registrar may strike the IC off the register, impose restoration fees, and revoke the license of any inbound trust or corporate service provider that facilitated the sham arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the debts and liabilities of the struck-off company under the International Companies Act. Civil courts may pierce the corporate veil, order restitution, impose travel bans, and, in egregious cases, direct custodial sentences for contempt or fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence or obtain and maintain beneficial ownership records; providing financial portfolio tracking or payment processing services without a Samoan AML compliance framework, or routing suspicious funds through payment rails such as Stripe or Apple IAP without transaction monitoring.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act: corporate fines up to WST 200,000 and imprisonment of officers up to 5 years. The licensed registered agent may also be subject to regulatory suspension or permanent revocation of its license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal liability where culpable knowledge is proven. Courts may impose personal asset freezes, travel bans, and civil restitution orders. Directors of the registered agent and the IC can be jointly and severally liable for AML penalties if they authorized or failed to prevent the breach.
